findings.location: rounds/c1/binding.json /nonClaims; rounds/c1/README.md 'Non-claims'; linux_probe_interface.py NON_CLAIMS; DESIGN.rev1.md section 2 nonClaims
findings.finding: The MANIFEST has two nonClaims. The record and README carry the first (form only, no acceptance by R12) and the ownerNotes, but drop the second: "R12 vendors this contract back later; until then R12's own files remain authoritative." Nothing in the record or README states that R12's files stay authoritative until R12 vendors v1/ back, and the README's reader duties ('the kit takes the form from v1/ ... never from R12') read without that limit.
findings.requiredChange: Add a fourth non-claim carrying MANIFEST nonClaims[1] (for example R12_FILES_AUTHORITATIVE_UNTIL_VENDORED), list it in the README and in the model's NON_CLAIMS, and add its vector; or obtain a monitor ruling that it is deliberately not carried and say so in the README.

findings.finding: The model checks the non-claim ids, their order, closed rows and non-empty text only. Planted: NOT_ACCEPTANCE rewritten to 'A probe kit built from this contract is accepted by R12.' is accepted with []; FORM_ONLY set to a single space is accepted with []. The refusal text 'the non-claims are not exactly as stated' claims more than the check does.
findings.requiredChange: Pin each non-claim's exact text in the model (they are build constants) and refuse any difference; add a vector for a changed text and one for a whitespace-only text.

findings.location: linux_probe_interface.py _check, ownerDecisions block; README 'Owner decisions are quoted ...'
findings.finding: The model accepts an empty ownerDecisions list, a record with the R12-ACCEPTANCE-RULES row dropped, and a changed Q-PK-6 quote (all planted, all []). Keeping the quote-in-section check at the build follows LPK-0's S3-6, but the two {id, quote} rows are constants the model can pin without reading the decision record, so the record can lose its decision binding while the layer's model still passes.
findings.requiredChange: Pin exactly the two rows (Q-PK-6 'Neutral contract (Recommended)', R12-ACCEPTANCE-RULES 'Keep them in R12 (Recommended)') in the model; add vectors for an empty list and a changed quote.

findings.finding: The README says 'a member of the wrong type refuses with the shape text'. Planted: slot 263.0 (a float) is accepted with [] because 263.0 != 263 is false in Python; source given as a list refuses with the MANIFEST text; nonClaims given as an object refuses with the claims text. Only the first is a pass, but the README claim is not what the model does.
findings.requiredChange: Check top-level member types first (slot with type(x) is int, the strings with str, files/reviews/ownerDecisions/nonClaims as lists, source/placeholderBinding as objects) and refuse with the shape text; add a vector for slot 263.0. Otherwise reword the README.

findings.location: linux_probe_interface.py valid() and keywords(); README and DESIGN 'Any other keyword refuses, so a later schema is never validated silently in part'
findings.finding: valid() treats every boolean subschema as false and keywords() does not look at boolean subschemas. For a later schema with if: true, then is silently skipped (probe: ours valid, jsonschema 4.24.0 invalid, 2020-12 invalid) and the keyword gate passes. items/properties/allOf: true are over-strict. The bound schema has 27 boolean subschemas, all false, which valid() handles correctly, so the bound result is unaffected; the README's 'never validated silently in part' claim is not true in general.
findings.requiredChange: Treat true as always valid and false as never valid in valid(), or refuse any boolean true subschema at the keyword gate; add a vector with if: true.

findings.finding: Validator disagreement with jsonschema 4.24.0 and 2020-12: an integer-valued float (10.0) fails type integer and const 10 in ours, but is valid in 2020-12. Ours is stricter only; the bound instance holds no floats, so its result is unaffected.
findings.requiredChange: None for v1. Optionally state 'numbers with a fraction part, including .0, are refused' in the README, or align is_type/same with 2020-12.

findings.finding: pattern uses Python re.search, where $ also matches before a final line feed; ECMA-262 (the 2020-12 regex dialect) does not. Ours and jsonschema 4.24.0 agree (commit + LF is valid in both); 2020-12 refuses it. The bound instance's only strings ending in LF are /http/headerRules/lineSeparator and /terminator, both const positions, so the bound result is unaffected. The other patterns use ASCII classes, anchors and bounded repeats only (judged on paper).
findings.requiredChange: None for v1. Optionally refuse a pattern match that relies on $ before a final LF, and say the validator uses Python re.

findings.finding: The model checks each digest against the bytes but does not pin the monitor's four digests: a consistent re-digest of a conforming but altered interface (a check renamed; files, MANIFEST.files, MANIFEST digest and interfaceSha256 re-pinned) is accepted. The MANIFEST source is compared on the record's four members only, so a MANIFEST whose source gains a member is accepted (planted). Both are by design covered elsewhere: build.py pins the four digests, and section 5 binds every era file by digest and requires the four v1/ files byte-identical.
findings.requiredChange: At mechanics, make the layer pin binding.json's sha256 and the four monitor digests (or add them to the model as constants), and compare the MANIFEST source exactly.

findings.finding: Each vector pins one refusal text by presence, not the full sorted list. 9 of 18 negatives return extra texts; the five schema-violation vectors and the unsupported-keyword vector also refuse on sha256 because their override bytes are not re-digested, so they do not isolate the validator from the digest check.
findings.requiredChange: Pin each vector's full refusal list, and add re-digested conformance and keyword vectors that refuse with exactly their own text.

findings.location: linux_probe_interface.py check() and the keyword gate
findings.finding: Two robustness gaps. A wrongly digested MANIFEST with 200000-deep nesting raises RecursionError out of check() instead of refusing (check catches TypeError to re.error only). A schema whose $schema names draft-07 passes the gate and is validated with 2020-12 meaning.
findings.requiredChange: Catch RecursionError (or parse a file only after its digest matches) so every input refuses; refuse unless $schema is the 2020-12 URI.

findings.location: DESIGN.rev1.md sections 1 and 5 (the tests, the three catalogs)
findings.finding: The design does not name the test paths or the three catalogs. Placement was checked with assumed test names (tests/test_linux_probe_interface.py, tests/test_validate_linux_probe_interface.py, tests/test_linux_probe_interface_oracle.py): any tests/ path outside tests/fixtures/zero-bill/ is data at 2043cc27, and an oracle test named test_*oracle*.py is ORACLE_TESTS. The catalogs are existing files and were not checked.
findings.requiredChange: Name the test paths and the catalogs in the mechanics brief and re-run check_coverage on them before the pre-check, as DESIGN section 1 says.
